inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30 June 2026: 8,820.9m ordinary shares in issue (H1 2026 note 10) less c.30m treasury/EBT shares plus 35m dilutive potential shares (H1 2026 note 7 dilutive table) = c.8,826m. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the £500m/yr buyback is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and is value-neutral here.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement, share-based payment add-back £86m (kpis StockBasedComp); no separate equity-award tax line disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0). Not stripped: interest received (£60m) sits in investing activities, outside the OCF-based reported_fcf, and the company is net-debt, so there is no cash pile to double-count.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP), so fx_rate 100 converts model GBP/share to quote pence. Parity check 2026-10-09: 349.2p x 2 ordinary shares per NYSE ADS = GBP 6.984 x GBPUSD 1.3233 = USD 9.24 vs HLN ADS close USD 9.32 (0.9% gap, intraday drift). Source: Yahoo Finance chart API.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP, the flows' currency. Cost of equity c.7.75%: UK 10y gilt c.4.5% + 5.0% ERP x beta 0.65 (defensive consumer-health staple). Pre-tax cost of debt c.3.7% (FY2025 finance costs £340m on c.£9.3bn average gross debt; investment grade Baa1/BBB), 2.8% after 24.5% tax. Weights c.80/20 on market cap c.£31bn vs net debt £7.5bn gives 6.8%; rounded up to 7.0% as the house figure. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, in the flows and the probability weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. Lease liabilities (£163m at 30 June 2026) are already inside Haleon's own net-debt definition, so net_debt £7,513m carries them once. Lease principal (£60m FY2025, in financing) is NOT deducted from the flows; D&A includes right-of-use depreciation; ongoing lease-asset renewal is charged as +0.55pp of revenue inside capex_pct_path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%), so non-controlling interests are charged once via the equity bridge: NCI book value £60m at 30 June 2026 deducted. NCI profit share is £12m/yr (FY2025), immaterial; the TSKF China JV stake was raised to 88% in 2025 (£174m paid).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, non-US consumer staple -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations). Haleon is a GBP-reporting consumer-health operating company with real free cash flow, net debt and EBITDA, so the default engine applies; no bank/REIT/LIC adaptation. ANCHORS: fy0 FY2025 (calendar 2025); year 1 of the projection is FY2026 (3-5% organic growth, high-single-digit adj. operating profit growth guided, reaffirmed 30 July 2026). Net debt and shares from the H1 2026 interim (30 June 2026). FCF BASIS: reported_fcf = OCF £2,634m - PPE capex £322m - intangibles £91m = £2,221m, pre-interest (Haleon classifies interest paid in financing and interest received in investing, so OCF is unlevered). Owner FCF = 2,221 - 86 SBC = £2,135m. Haleon's own 'free cash flow' (£1,913m) is post-interest and is NOT the base. FY2025 reported owner FCF (19.4% margin) was flattered by a working-capital inflow (OCF +£333m YoY) and cash tax paid of only £439m (c.17% of adjusted EBIT); the forward build charges a normalised 24-24.5% cash tax on EBIT, so year-1 owner FCF margin is c.15% - that gap is deliberate, not an error. MARGIN BASIS: ebitda_margin_path is adjusted EBITDA (FY2025 25.7%, H1 2026 27.0%) LESS the cash cost of restructuring/adjusting items (c.1.5pp FY2026 for the £175-200m operating-model restructuring, 1.0pp FY2027, 0.5pp ongoing as a permanent cost of doing business), so the flows are not on the company's flattering adjusted basis. CAPEX: FY2025 3.74% of revenue (PPE £322m + intangibles £91m) is elevated by the c.£240m China/India Oral Health site programme announced H1 2026; path runs 4.3% (incl. 0.55pp lease renewal) easing to 3.6% mature. SHARE COUNT held flat; buybacks (£654m FY2025, £500m allocated 2026, £457m done by H1) exceed SBC so the flat count is funded by the repurchaser, not a modelling convention. WORKING CAPITAL: Haleon's trade payables (c.£3.4bn) roughly equal inventory plus receivables, so growth is approximately working-capital neutral; wc_capture 0. TERMINAL: cap 18x FCF in base, matching today's EV/owner-FCF of c.18x, so the base assumes no multiple expansion; 20x bull, 15x bear.

equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 balance sheet, 30 June 2026; flows are 100% consolidated so NCI is deducted once here

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management medium-term guidance (4-6% organic) taken at the LOW end: FY2025 organic growth was 3.0% and FY2026 is guided 3-5%. Equity CAGR is not usable as the primary signal post-demerger.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (3y +0.2%, 4y -11.2%) diverges >30% from revenue (+0.5% 3y, +3.7% 4y) and EPS (+17.2% 3y). The divergence is capital-structure driven: the July 2022 demerger from GSK stripped c.£10bn from equity (FY2021 £26.4bn -> FY2022 £16.3bn), then dividends and £1.3bn of buybacks over FY2024-25 held book value flat while earnings compounded. EPS growth is also flattered by the FY2022-23 trough (separation and amortisation charges). None of these series is a clean forward growth proxy, hence the guidance-anchored selection.
historical_growth.notes: Only 5 fiscal years (FY2021-FY2025) are available; FY2021 is the pre-demerger carve-out basis, so the '5yr' figures are 4-year CAGRs FY2021-FY2025. Owner-FCF series (reported pre-interest FCF less SBC): FY2021 1,058; FY2022 1,720; FY2023 1,688; FY2024 1,881; FY2025 2,135. Owner-FCF 3y CAGR 7.5% vs reported 8.6%: SBC grew from £15m to £86m as post-demerger LTIPs matured, so about one point of the reported FCF growth was paid in stock. FY2025 owner FCF also carries a working-capital inflow and a low cash-tax year; the component build normalises both.

base.narrative: FY2026 reported growth 3.0% (organic c.3.8%, low-mid of the 3-5% guide, FX roughly flat, weak H1 cold & flu), then 4% through FY2030 at the low end of the 4-6% medium-term algorithm before fading to 2.5% nominal. Adjusted EBITDA margin expands c.40-50bps/yr (gross-margin productivity programme plus £175-200m operating-model savings) from 25.7% to c.28.3% by FY2030, less a permanent 0.5pp restructuring charge after the 2026-27 one-off costs roll through. Cash tax normalises to the guided 24.5% adjusted ETR. Capex elevated through FY2027 for the China/India Oral Health sites then settles at 3.6% incl. lease renewal.

bull.narrative: The 'Win as One' algorithm is delivered: North America returns to sustained growth, emerging markets (India, China, LatAm) and affordable price-point packs lift organic growth to the middle of the 4-6% range (5-5.5% FY2027-29), Oral Health keeps compounding at high-single digits, and a normal cold & flu season removes the respiratory drag. The full £800m supply-chain programme plus operating-model savings push adjusted EBITDA margin to c.30% by FY2031 (29.5% after the ongoing restructuring charge). Terminal cap 20x reflects a defensive compounder re-rating toward staples peers.

bear.narrative: The medium-term 4-6% algorithm is quietly abandoned: North America VMS and Pain Relief stay promotional against a merged Kimberly-Clark/Kenvue, weak cold & flu seasons recur, and the 2026-27 operating-model overhaul disrupts commercial execution, holding organic growth at 2-2.5%. Productivity savings are competed away in price and reinvested in A&P, so adjusted EBITDA margin only edges to c.26.5% (26.0% after a persistent restructuring charge). Cash tax at the 25% UK statutory rate. Capex stays elevated at c.3.8% as the growth projects underdeliver. No solvency issue at 2.5x leverage, so WACC is unchanged; terminal cap 15x and 2.0% growth price a permanently ex-growth staple.

scenario_narratives.base: Haleon delivers the low end of its own medium-term algorithm: c.4% organic growth through FY2030 (after a 3% FY2026), 40-50bps/yr of adjusted margin expansion from the £800m productivity programme and the new operating model, cash tax at the guided 24.5%, and capex easing after the China/India site build. The base case takes management at its word on margins but discounts the top line, because FY2025 (+3.0%) and FY2026 (3-5% guided) both sit below the 4-6% target. Terminal multiple capped at today's c.18x EV/owner-FCF, so no re-rating is assumed.
scenario_narratives.bull: Growth re-accelerates to the middle of the 4-6% range on North America recovery, emerging-market volume (India distribution doubling, China e-commerce, affordable packs) and Oral Health share gains; the productivity and operating-model programmes deliver in full, taking adjusted EBITDA margin to c.30%; a defensive compounder with a deleveraged balance sheet re-rates to a 20x FCF exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: Top line stalls at 2-2.5% as the promotional environment in North America and a stronger Kimberly-Clark/Kenvue competitor absorb pricing, respiratory stays weak and the 2026-27 restructuring distracts execution; margin gains are reinvested rather than banked; the market treats Haleon as an ex-growth leveraged staple at 15x FCF. No going-concern or covenant dimension: the balance sheet (2.5x net debt/EBITDA, investment grade, maturities to 2052) survives the bear case comfortably, so the downside is valuation, not solvency.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; moved to 25/50/25. Bear raised from 15% to 25% because the company has already missed its 4-6% growth algorithm in FY2025 and guided below it for FY2026, so 'growth undershoots' is not a tail but a live path, and the Zantac indemnification claims from GSK/Pfizer, while rejected and largely settled upstream, remain an unquantified contingent tail. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: North America recovery, emerging-market volume delivery, and full productivity-programme capture without reinvestment. Base held at 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Haleon is a defensive, cash-generative consumer-health compounder whose value rests on 3-5% growth plus steady margin expansion, discounted at a GBP WACC of 7%. The valuation is deliberately built on owner FCF (SBC expensed, restructuring charged, cash tax normalised to 24.5%, interest excluded from the base because net debt is deducted in the bridge) rather than the company's adjusted and post-interest 'free cash flow'. Base-case terminal value is capped at the current c.18x EV/owner-FCF so the house number assumes no re-rating; with WACC at 7% and a 15% hurdle the entry price will sit well below intrinsic value, which is the arithmetic of demanding 15% from a 7%-risk asset and not a signal of mispricing.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value dominates (long-duration, slow-growth flows at a 7% WACC): a 1pp move in WACC or terminal growth moves per-share value by double digits in pence.

Margin-expansion delivery: the base case banks c.2pp of adjusted EBITDA margin from productivity and operating-model savings; if those are competed away in price or reinvested in A&P the base collapses toward the bear.
Organic growth has undershot the 4-6% target in FY2025 and FY2026 guidance; a formal downgrade of the medium-term algorithm would move the base growth path down by 1pp.
Respiratory/cold & flu seasonality adds +/-1pp of annual growth noise that the model treats as mean-reverting.
Zantac/ranitidine indemnification claims from GSK and Pfizer (rejected by Haleon, upstream cases mostly settled) are not in the flows; a successful claim would be a bridge deduction.
FX: c.33% North America, c.25% EUR; GBP translation moved FY2026 guidance from a 1% headwind to slightly positive within five months. The model is in GBP at constant currency.

Share count: 8,826m is a 30 June 2026 figure; the ongoing £500m buyback lowers it by c.1.5%/yr, which the flat-count convention does not credit (buybacks are treated as the SBC-neutralising mechanism).
